name: Coligny

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Coligny is a Continental Celtic site in the southeast of France. An artifact found there matters to students of the Celts. The bronze pieces of the Coligny Calendar record five years in a lunar year of 12 months and 355 days. Every 30 months the scheme adds a 30 day month to pull the count back in step with the sun. The calendar came from a shrine to the Romano-Celtic Mars and likely served a rite. It is the only Celtic calendar known to archaeology.

okr.objective: Coligny holds the only Celtic calendar known to archaeology.
key_results: The Coligny Calendar is made of bronze fragments.
It records a lunar year and an added month every 30 months.
It was found in a shrine to the Romano-Celtic Mars.
